# Parakeets & Budgies for Sale in the UK

Parakeets & Budgerigars are available through Crownwing by enquiry. If you are comparing budgies or other small parrots for sale in the UK, ask which species and individual birds are available now, with current photographs, ages and prices. A budgerigar, ringneck, lovebird and parrotlet need different care plans; identify the bird before choosing housing or companions.

## Available by enquiry

Parakeets & Budgerigars are available through Crownwing. Individual birds change regularly. Contact us for current birds, photographs and prices.

## Specify the species and individual

Name the type you are asking about and confirm which species the individual actually is. Ask what is known about its age, identity and any sex information, while recognising that not every detail may be established. The phrase 'small parrot' is not enough to judge adult size, suitable enclosure or expected voice.

Ask about the bird's usual diet, activity, social preferences and response to people. A budgerigar accustomed to other birds may have different needs from a hand-focused parrotlet or a ringneck used to a larger setup. Find out which behaviour is observed and which is merely an assumption based on the species.

## Availability and background

Crownwing welcomes enquiries across this group, but that does not confirm that any particular species or bird is available now. Ask clearly which individual, if any, can be discussed and how availability is confirmed. Do not assume a list of examples represents current stock.

If hand-rearing is part of your question, ask what is known about the particular bird's rearing and weaning history. Ask what company it has been used to and how it spends a normal day. A small bird's history matters; neither size nor a particular rearing method guarantees that it will welcome handling.

## Budgie and parakeet prices: compare the exact bird

Request the current price for the specific species and bird, and ask exactly what, if anything, is included. There is no single price for such a varied group. Budget for suitable enclosure dimensions and bar spacing, safe perches, flight opportunities, appropriate food and enrichment that can be replaced as it is used.

Set up the home around the confirmed species rather than buying equipment based on a generic small-bird label. A ringneck needs a different amount of space from a budgerigar, and tiny feet require appropriate perch and bar dimensions. Ask which foods and equipment are familiar so you can plan a manageable transition.

## Handover and the right household match

Ask what information can accompany the bird, how collection is arranged and which daily routines are established. Confirm any payment, reservation and collection details directly. If something is unknown, note that clearly; do not treat a broad category description as evidence about an individual.

Describe your household, experience, available space and the sound level you can live with. Ask how this bird's social needs may fit the time people are away and whether it is used to other birds. Families should agree who is responsible for daily care and how children will be supervised. Decide only after matching species-specific needs to your real routine.

Can budgerigar flock guidance be applied to an Indian ringneck?

Do not assume that social patterns are identical across the group. Identify the exact species and ask about the individual bird's established company and routine before planning companions or daily interaction.

Can two small parrot species share one enclosure?

Different species should not be presumed compatible because their bodies are small. Consider their adult size, behaviour and resource needs, and plan separate safe accommodation unless compatibility and management have been carefully established.
